name: Mali

findings.summary: Mali's cabinet approved awarding Huawei a 15-month, roughly FCFA 35.2bn contract, fully financed by China Exim Bank, for 1,300+ km of fibre on three corridors plus government network modernisation, a Bamako data centre and videoconferencing.
findings.analyst_inference: OSIRIS republishes the same Ecofin story, so not independent; uncorroborated tier 3 is low. Body gives FCFA 35,213,172,169 vs headline 34bn; not converted to USD (no source-date rate taken). Pre-2020 and completion/operation not confirmed, so still_current null. Bundled with MLI-002 (same contract).

findings.summary: The same Huawei broadband contract, financed by China Exim Bank, included a security and road-traffic video surveillance system and associated monitoring rooms.
findings.analyst_inference: Same single-origin reporting as MLI-001. Whether the surveillance component was delivered, and its scale, is not established; still_current null.

findings.summary: Mali signed a XOF 93.8bn concessional China Exim Bank loan for Mali Numérique 2020: an 817 km fibre backbone, government GPON and a secure state wireless network, built by CITCC; parliament authorised it in November 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4: financing agreement signed and ratified; build completion not confirmed. Source names CITCC (Chinese state-owned telecom contractor) and '12 OSN 3500 terminals' - OSN 3500 is, to the analyst's knowledge, a Huawei OptiX product line, suggesting Huawei equipment, but no source states the vendor, so controller is CITCC. Value not converted.

findings.summary: Mali's cabinet approved a US$117.3m contract with CITCC to extend the national fibre network to Mopti, Koro, Timbuktu, Gao, Ansongo and Labenzanga over two years.
findings.analyst_inference: Developing Telecoms cites Ecofin, so the two are not independent. Equipment vendor and financier not stated; pole prc on CITCC as integrator, reviewer may prefer null until vendor known. Completion not confirmed.

findings.local_actor: Société Malienne de Transmission et de Diffusion (SMTD)
findings.summary: At FOCAC, state broadcaster-transmitter SMTD signed an MOU with Huawei for the Mali Numérique programme covering camera monitoring in Bamako and regional capitals, 1,000 km more fibre and a Tier III national data centre.
findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding MOU, tier 1. Coded on applications as the surveillance component is the most specific; fibre and data-centre components overlap MLI-006, where Huawei's role is unconfirmed. Date inferred from 'yesterday' in a 4 Sept 2024 article.

findings.controller: Government of Mali (Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy and Modernisation of Administration)
findings.summary: Malian authorities inaugurated a Tier III national data centre in Bamako on 31 January 2026 to host e-government platforms and state databases; builder, financier, size and cost were not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: State owner-operator, so domestic. DCD notes Huawei had earlier been linked to a Tier III centre (MLI-005) but was not mentioned at launch; builder left null. Tier 4 (in service at launch; utilisation at scale unconfirmed). Corroboration may rest on one government announcement.

findings.local_actor: Centre de coordination et de gestion des crises (CECOGEC), Prime Minister's Office / Ministry of Security
findings.summary: A modernised national crisis-management operations room, backed technically and financially by Huawei, opened in September 2026, aggregating over 74 video feeds with a video wall, radio geolocation and emergency-call handling, with video coverage extended to Ségou, Sikasso and Mopti.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S3 source relaying Malian state agency AMAP. Pole prc on equipment rule, assuming Huawei-supplied system; exact equipment and terms (donation or sale) not stated. Possibly the delivery of MLI-005's camera component - not established.

findings.reversal_of: Unlicensed Starlink terminal use in Mali
findings.summary: Mali's junta ordered Starlink terminals dismantled and banned nationwide, citing unauthorised use by NGOs, individuals and armed separatist and jihadist groups in the north and east.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 assigned to the reversed thing: unlicensed informal Starlink use, never an authorised service. Security rationale coded geopolitical. still_current false: lifted October 2024 (MLI-009). Both reports may share wire origin.

findings.summary: Mali's Council of Ministers lifted the Starlink ban, allowing kit import and sale for six months while a regulatory framework and user registration platform are set up.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 as a time-limited provisional authorisation, not a licence. Whether a licence or framework followed after April 2025 not checked; still_current null.
